title: Conjecture 2
context_text: A colouring has clustering $k$ if each monochromatic component has at most $k$ vertices. The clustered chromatic number $\chi_\star(\mathcal{G})$ of a class $\mathcal{G}$ is the minimum $c$ such that for some $k$ every graph of $\mathcal{G}$ is $c$-colourable with clustering $k$; the defective chromatic number $\chi_\Delta(\mathcal{G})$ is the minimum $c$ such that for some $d$ every graph of $\mathcal{G}$ is $c$-colourable with monochromatic components of maximum degree at most $d$. An $H$-model in $G$ is a family $(T_x:x\in V(H))$ of vertex-disjoint subtrees with an edge between $T_x$ and $T_y$ for each $xy\in E(H)$; it is odd if some $2$-colouring of the union of the trees and these connecting edges properly colours each $T_x$ and has a monochromatic edge between $T_x$ and $T_y$ for each $xy\in E(H)$. $H$ is an odd-minor of $G$ if $G$ has an odd $H$-model; $\mathcal{G}_H^{\mathrm{odd}}$ is the class of graphs with no $H$ odd-minor and $\mathcal{G}_H$ the class of $H$-minor-free graphs. The connected tree-depth $\overline{\mathrm{td}}(H)$ is the minimum vertex-height (number of vertices on a longest root-to-leaf path) of a rooted tree $T$ on $V(H)$ such that $H$ is a subgraph of the closure of $T$ (pairs in ancestor–descendant relation); it equals the tree-depth unless $H$ has two components of maximum tree-depth, in which case it is one more. For minors, $\overline{\mathrm{td}}(H)-1=\chi_\Delta(\mathcal{G}_H)\le\chi_\star(\mathcal{G}_H)\le3\overline{\mathrm{td}}(H)-3$ (Ossona de Mendez, Oum and Wood; Norin, Scott, Seymour and Wood; Liu), and Norin et al. conjectured $\chi_\star(\mathcal{G}_H)\le2\overline{\mathrm{td}}(H)-2$, which is tight for some $H$. The authors prove the odd-minor analogue $\overline{\mathrm{td}}(H)-1\le\chi_\Delta(\mathcal{G}_H^{\mathrm{odd}})\le\chi_\star(\mathcal{G}_H^{\mathrm{odd}})\le3\cdot2^{\overline{\mathrm{td}}(H)}-4$; also $\chi_\star(\mathcal{G}_H^{\mathrm{odd}})\le3\chi_\Delta(\mathcal{G}_H^{\mathrm{odd}})$ by a result of Liu and Wood.
